title: Chili con carne
intro: Beef and kidney beans slow-simmered with cumin and smoked paprika: thick and warming.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and soften the chopped onion and pepper over medium heat.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add the garlic and beef, turn up the heat and brown it, breaking it up, until no longer pink and lightly colored.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Stir in cumin, paprika, cayenne, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, water and salt, bring to a boil, set the lid ajar and simmer gently, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Add tomatoes, half the water and salt, lock the pressure cooker lid and cook 20 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add the beans and cook uncovered until the chili is thick and rich.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Taste, adjust salt and heat and let it rest off the heat before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Melt in a square of dark chocolate at the end: it rounds out the flavor without tasting of it.
Serve with white rice, sour cream and tortilla chips, or spooned over a baked potato.
It's even better the next day and freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Shakshuka
intro: Eggs gently poached in a pepper, tomato and harissa sauce, served in the pan.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide lidded pan and cook the onion and sliced peppers over medium heat until soft and sweet.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add sliced garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, season with salt and simmer uncovered until thickened.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Make 4 hollows in the sauce with a spoon, crack an egg into each and season lightly.
Cover and cook on low until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Scatter over chopped herbs and pepper and bring the pan straight to the table.

tips.t: Serve with warm bread or pita to mop up the sauce (skip it to keep the dish gluten-free).
Crumble 80 g of feta over the sauce before covering for an even tastier pan.

title: Jambalaya
intro: Louisiana rice with chicken, smoked sausage and shrimp, all cooked in one pot.

steps.t: In a wide lidded pot, brown the sliced sausage in the oil until golden, then lift it out.
steps.label: Sausage

steps.t: In the same fat, brown the diced chicken until golden on all sides, then lift it out.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add diced onion, pepper and celery and cook until soft.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add garlic, paprika, thyme, oregano, cayenne and bay for 1 minute, then pour in tomatoes and hot stock (store-bought is fine) and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, return chicken and sausage, salt, cover and cook on low without stirring; the chicken finishes cooking in the rice.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Tuck the shrimp into the rice, cover and cook until pink and the rice is tender.
steps.label: Shrimp

steps.t: Turn off the heat and rest, covered. Remove the bay leaves and top with sliced scallions.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Don't stir while the rice cooks: it stays fluffy and forms a light crust on the bottom.
A dash of Louisiana-style hot sauce at the table is practically mandatory.

title: Italian beef stew with potatoes
intro: Beef braised slowly in wine and stock with potatoes: Italy's winter Sunday dish.

steps.t: Cut the meat into 4 cm chunks and pat dry. Brown it in batches in hot oil in a heavy pot until well crusted.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lower the heat, add chopped onion, carrot and celery and let them soften.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Return all the meat, pour in the wine and let it bubble off, scraping the bottom.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Add tomato paste, rosemary, bay and hot stock (store-bought or cube is fine) to cover. Put the lid on and cook on low.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add tomato paste, herbs and stock to half-cover the meat. Lock the lid and cook 25 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add peeled potato chunks and salt. Keep cooking, covered, until the potatoes are tender and the meat falls apart.
steps.label: Potatoes

pressure.t: Add the potato chunks and salt, lock the lid again and cook 8 more minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: If the sauce is too thin, uncover for the last minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Don't crowd the pot when browning: the meat should sizzle, not stew in its juices.
It's even better the next day: reheat gently with a ladle of stock.
Instead of potatoes, add peas for the last 15 minutes, as they do in Tuscany.

title: Vegetable and chickpea tagine
intro: Squash, carrots and chickpeas stewed with Moroccan spices and dried apricots.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy casserole and soften the sliced onion over medium heat.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add garlic, ras el hanout, ginger and turmeric and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrots cut in thick sticks and squash in large chunks and turn them in the spices.
Add tomatoes, stock (store-bought is fine), chickpeas, halved apricots and salt. Cover and simmer until the veg are tender.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Uncover and let the sauce reduce over medium heat.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Finish with chopped coriander and toasted almonds.

tips.t: Serve with steamed couscous; for gluten-free, with rice or quinoa.
A chopped preserved lemon rind stirred in at the end gives the authentic aroma.

title: Ciambotta
intro: Southern Italy's summer stew: potatoes, peppers, eggplant and zucchini in tomato.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide pot and soften the sliced onion and garlic over medium heat.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add the potatoes in 2 cm cubes and stir them around in the oil.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Add pepper strips and eggplant cubes, salt and cook, stirring often, until they start to soften.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add zucchini chunks, chopped tomatoes and basil. Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
steps.label: Stew

steps.t: If it's too liquid, uncover for the last minutes. Turn off and let it rest: it's even better warm than hot.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Crack 4 eggs over the hot stew for the last 5 minutes and cover: it becomes an even heartier meal.
Serve with toasted country bread, and shaved aged pecorino for those who want it.
